---
title: CoreWeave training and rollouts
---

## Submit a training job to SUNK

The `coreweave` cloud provider submits complete Axolotl jobs to an existing
CoreWeave SUNK cluster through Slurm and Pyxis/Enroot. Run it on a login node, or
set `ssh_host` to an authenticated SSH host alias. It uses `sbatch`, `srun`, and
shared storage; Ray is not required.

Copy `examples/cloud/coreweave.yaml` and set the partition, shared directory,
container image, and optional account/QoS for your cluster. The image must include
Axolotl and its training dependencies. Use a shared `.sqsh` image, a registry image
tag, or `image_build` with a registry tag. Built images are pushed before submission.

```bash
axolotl train train.yaml --cloud examples/cloud/coreweave.yaml --launcher torchrun
```

The launcher stages the YAML and bootstrap files in a unique directory under
`shared_dir`. Each allocated node starts one launcher, which starts one worker per
GPU. Slurm supplies node ranks and the rendezvous host. Set `nodes` and
`gpus_per_node` in the cloud YAML; do not pass conflicting launcher topology flags.
The Python launcher is supported for one GPU on one node.

Relative `output_dir` values are resolved inside the job directory. Absolute
outputs must be beneath `shared_dir` or an explicit shared `mounts` entry. Datasets,
resume checkpoints, custom reward modules, and referenced config files must be in
the image or on those mounts; local working directories are not uploaded. Use
absolute cluster paths for such files. Place cluster-specific NCCL/UCX settings in
`env`; the provider does not assume InfiniBand or RoCE network interfaces.

For credentials, `env_file` points to a shell environment file readable on the
allocated node. It is mounted read-only and sourced inside the container before starting Python.
Explicit `env` values take precedence over the file and image defaults.
`MASTER_ADDR` and `MASTER_PORT` remain launcher-owned. SSH submission does
not forward your laptop's environment. Credentials and service access must be
configured on SUNK, and private image pulls need Enroot authentication there.

Submission returns the Slurm job ID and persistent log path. It does not wait for
training to finish. Use `squeue -j JOB_ID`, `sacct -j JOB_ID`, or `scancel JOB_ID`
on the login node to inspect or cancel a job. An uncertain submission is not
automatically retried. `dry_run: true` validates and previews submission without
staging files, building an image, or allocating resources.

See [Run veRL on SUNK](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/sunk/tutorials/verl-on-sunk)
for shared-storage and container setup. The cloud launcher can run ordinary SFT
and RL configurations independently of Dedicated Inference.

## Publish checkpoints to Dedicated Inference

The CoreWeave plugin publishes saved full-model checkpoints to an existing
Dedicated Inference deployment with hot-loading enabled. The first publication
is a full Hugging Face checkpoint. Subsequent publications use Slime-compatible
byte-level XOR deltas, Zstandard compression, and Adler-32 checksums. A new full
checkpoint starts the chain after 128 deltas, or after restarting the trainer.

Install the upload dependency with `pip install 'axolotl[coreweave]'`. Configure
AWS credentials for CoreWeave AI Object Storage and set `CW_API_TOKEN` to an
Inference Admin token. The deployment's immutable hot-load bucket and path prefix
must match the configuration below. Grant the inference service read access and
the uploader write access to that bucket.

```yaml
plugins:
  - axolotl.integrations.coreweave.CoreWeavePlugin

coreweave:
  deployment_id: your-deployment-id
  gateway_url: https://your-gateway-endpoint
  model: your-deployment-model-name
  bucket: your-checkpoint-bucket
  path_prefix: training/run-001
  s3_profile: cw
  # s3_endpoint_url: http://cwlota.com  # From a CoreWeave cluster
  max_deltas: 128
  timeout: 900
  async_publish: true

save_safetensors: true
save_steps: 100
```

The callback reads completed `checkpoint-N` saves containing either full HF
model weights and `config.json`, or standard LoRA adapters (see below). Quantized
adapters and distributed checkpoint formats without gathered HF weights or
adapter tensors are not supported. The original
training checkpoints remain usable for training resume. Delta artifacts are
inference weights, not optimizer or trainer-state checkpoints.

Checkpoint-save publishing runs in the background by default. Once the trainer
has written a checkpoint, the callback retains its files using hard links and
queues it. A single worker reads the saved tensors, writes the full/delta artifact,
uploads it, and waits for hot-loading while training continues. Hard links protect
queued checkpoints from `save_total_limit` rotation; filesystems without hard-link
support use a local copy before returning from the save callback.

Every queued checkpoint is published in order. The queue stores disk paths rather
than model snapshots, but retained files occupy disk space until publication
finishes. A slow service can therefore grow the disk backlog. The first worker
failure prevents later publications and is raised on the next training step or
save. Normal training completion drains the queue and reports any failure. On
training abort, teardown cancels queued work and joins the active publication.
Set `async_publish: false` for synchronous checkpoint-save publishing.

The queue is shared infrastructure in
`axolotl.core.checkpoint_publisher.BackgroundCheckpointPublisher`. Other integrations
can pass a `publish(directory, step)` callable, for example one that uploads files
directly to S3. The default retention function pins all checkpoint files, including
nested files; a custom `retain(source, queue_root)` callable can select a subset
with `retain_checkpoint(..., files=[...])`. Call `submit` after each completed save,
`check` at training boundaries, and `close` to drain publication. Abort handling
should call `close(cancel_pending=True)`. The CoreWeave subclass selects only HF
model or adapter files and loads tensors inside the worker.

Artifacts are stored under `output_dir/coreweave-checkpoints/` and uploaded under
unique checkpoint identities. Shards are uploaded before the index. Hot-loading
uses `PROMPT_CACHE_POLICY_RESET_ALL` and waits for operation completion and all
replica pages to report the target identity. Failure stops publication without
advancing the baseline. Keep the full baseline and all dependent deltas in object
storage; the plugin does not delete them. Full-model publication uses CPU memory
for both the previous and current model snapshots, plus shard encoding buffers.

### Publishing LoRA checkpoints

Add these settings to the checkpoint-publishing configuration above:

```yaml
base_model: your-org/your-bf16-base
revision_of_model: your-base-commit-sha
adapter: lora
bf16: true
```

The worker pins a private copy of the original base on first publication. Every
saved adapter is merged against that same base with the sharded LoRA merger on
CPU. A shard callback compares the resulting BF16 bytes with the last successfully
published merged shard and immediately encodes its XOR delta. The initial
publication and periodic chain resets contain full merged weights. Full artifacts
inherit the base model's shard sizes; `max_shard_size` bounds delta shard packing
except for individual tensors larger than that limit.

CPU memory scales with shard size, adapter size, and encoding buffers, rather than
two full models. An exact merged baseline stays on disk. Unchanged shards are hard
linked into the next baseline; changed shards are written before publication. The
old baseline is removed only after successful hot-loading. During publication,
allow disk space for the original base, committed and candidate merged baselines,
retained adapters, and publication artifacts. Publication artifacts are retained.

Only standard matrix LoRA on an unquantized BF16 base with a built-in Transformers
architecture is supported initially. Saves must contain `adapter_config.json` and
`adapter_model.safetensors`. DoRA, QLoRA, modified-base initializations, resized
embeddings, `modules_to_save`, trainable token rows, and fused parameter adapters
are rejected. LoRA publication currently applies to saved checkpoints;
`coreweave.rollouts: true` still requires full-model training.

Dense LoRA updates can alter every value in a targeted matrix. Delta compression
therefore depends on the actual merged bytes and is not guaranteed to beat a full
checkpoint. This path preserves those bytes exactly without accumulating rounding
error across adapter steps.

The default save callback publishes checkpoints. The client and
publisher can also be called by a training backend at rollout boundaries:
`CheckpointPublisher.publish(state_dict, model_config, step)` completes before
`CoreWeaveClient.sample(...)` is allowed. Sampling returns exact response token
IDs and aligned log probabilities. The gateway URL should be its origin, without
the `/v1` suffix.

## Use CoreWeave rollouts with GRPO

For synchronous, text-only GRPO, add `rollouts: true` to the same `coreweave` block:

```yaml
rl: grpo
coreweave:
  # Include the deployment and storage settings above.
  rollouts: true
trl:
  use_vllm: false
  num_generations: 4
  temperature: 1.0
  top_p: 1.0
  max_completion_length: 256
  # Configure reward_funcs as for ordinary Axolotl GRPO.
```

The ordinary Axolotl GRPO trainer computes rewards, gradients, and optimizer
updates. The plugin replaces generation through TRL's rollout function. It gathers
the current full model state on all training ranks and publishes on rank zero
before each new optimizer step's rollout round, including the first round.
All ranks wait for the hot-load and replica checks before generation starts.
Requests complete before ranks leave the rollout function, so an update cannot
overlap the previous round's requests. The save callback is disabled in this mode;
regular training checkpoints continue to follow the training save schedule.
`async_publish` applies to checkpoint-save publishing only. GRPO rollout
publication remains synchronous so sampling cannot use an incompletely loaded
policy.

Use conversational dataset prompts containing text-only system, user, and
assistant messages. Chat templating, including reasoning/thinking options in
`trl.chat_template_kwargs`, happens locally. The client sends the resulting integer
`prompt` to `/v1/completions` and uses exactly those prompt IDs for training. The
deployment must use the same tokenizer vocabulary and support token-input
completions plus `return_tokens_as_token_ids`. This is supported by upstream
[Dynamo's completion API](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/blob/main/lib/llm/src/protocols/openai/completions.rs),
but availability through your CoreWeave gateway must be verified for its runtime
version. Unsupported endpoints fail explicitly; there is no chat or text
retokenization fallback. Responses must supply `choices[].token_ids` or exact
`token_id:N` entries in completion logprobs. Avoid concurrent publishers
and other traffic to the same deployment when requiring on-policy rounds.
Returned completion token IDs and log probabilities are used directly for
training. The integration enables pinned TRL's inference/training importance
correction during scoring and loss evaluation while keeping its vLLM generation
backend disabled. `trl.vllm_importance_sampling_correction` and its clipping/mode
settings retain their normal meanings; all four token/sequence mask/truncate
modes are supported. Liger loss kernels are currently unsupported. As in TRL,
VESPO requires `vllm_importance_sampling_correction: false`.

Sampling supports temperature and top-p; custom top-k, min-p, and
repetition penalties are rejected. Multimodal inputs, tools, adapters, asynchronous
GRPO, and context parallelism are not supported by this rollout integration.
Sharded training requires Accelerate to gather a full state dict; configure
DeepSpeed/FSDP accordingly. Live distributed GPU and CoreWeave validation is still
required before production use.

After a failed or uncertain hot-load, inspect its operation and replica state
before retrying. `CheckpointPublisher.recover(operation_id)` confirms a completed
operation targeting the pending identity and then advances the baseline. If an
upload failed, re-upload the pending artifact directory first and explicitly
submit its hot-load after resolving the failure. No automatic POST retries are
performed. Restarting the publisher starts a new full chain with a unique identity.

See [CoreWeave RL Rollouts](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/inference/rl-rollouts)
for deployment prerequisites and recovery, and
[Slime Delta Weight Sync](https://github.com/THUDM/slime/blob/main/docs/en/advanced/delta-weight-sync.md)
for the checkpoint format.
